question: Explain the circumstances in which the Assessing Officer may make a best judgment assessment under section 144 of the Income-tax Act, 1961, and the safeguards available to the assessee.

points.label: Failure to file a return
points.description: The assessee has not furnished the return required under section 139(1) and has not filed a belated or revised return.

points.label: Failure to comply with notices or directions
points.description: The assessee fails to comply with all the terms of a notice under section 142(1) or a direction for special audit under section 142(2A), or, having filed a return, fails to comply with a notice under section 143(2).

points.label: Nature of the assessment
points.description: The Assessing Officer takes into account all relevant material gathered and assesses total income or loss to the best of his judgment; the estimate must be honest and based on material, not arbitrary or punitive.
points.basis: Income-tax Act, 1961, section 144(1) and the settled principle that a best judgment must be fair and based on material

points.label: Opportunity of being heard
points.description: Before completing the assessment, the officer must serve a show cause notice asking why the assessment should not be made to the best of his judgment, except where a notice under section 142(1) was already issued before making the assessment.

points.label: Faceless procedure and appeal
points.description: In cases covered by the faceless assessment scheme, the assessment is made in a faceless manner; an assessee aggrieved by the order can appeal to the Commissioner (Appeals).
